title: Restriction of a single-source cocycle through exact strict-local functors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $s$ a geometric point, $g:S_{(s)}\to S$ its strict-henselization structural map, $K$ a bounded-below derived abelian etale sheaf, $L$ any cochain complex, $r:K\cong QL$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, $W$ etale over $S$, and $f:\mathbf Z[W]\to L^n$ a cycle. Let $\tau:\operatorname{sections}_W\to g^{-1}\circ\Gamma(S_{(s)},-)$ be any natural transformation. Use [def-weil-pbc-strict-local-injective-source-comparison] for the free-source Hom complex and degreewise evaluation, [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-restriction] for exact strict-local global sections, and [lem-weil-pbc-source-localized-cocycle-homology] for the constructed homology section (its definition does not require K-injectivity). Apply homology to the evaluated Hom-complex class, localize its degreewise image under $\tau$, factor exact global sections and inverse image through localization, transport by $r^{-1}$, and commute exact global sections with homology. The resulting element equals $\tau$ applied to the homology section of $f$, followed by the bounded-below exact-inverse-image homology comparison. No K-injectivity, stalk, or base-change mate is assumed.

proof.text: evaluate the single-source cocycle degreewise using sourceFreeSectionsComplexIso. Its class in the sections complex is the image of the Hom-complex class under the homology functor. Apply the natural transformation degreewise. Its naturality with respect to the cycle inclusion and homology projection identifies the restricted cycle with the image of the homology section. Exact inverse image and strict-local global sections preserve kernels and cokernels, hence identify this projection with the homology projection of the mapped complex. The quotient localization factorization is natural in the complex map; cancel its inverse with the homology factorization. The exact-functor homology comparisons are natural in r inverse, so transport along r gives precisely the displayed composite. Boundaries map to boundaries; thus the calculation descends to cohomology. Zero cycles and all integer degrees obey the same calculation. The transformation is arbitrary, so no stalk comparison is used.
